sections.content:
Timer: p=9, W=55. Total actions so far: ACTION7 (initial probe), LEFT, RIGHT, MOUSE×7 (1+6), ACTION7 (pocket). Total = 11 actions. But p=9. Hmm: 11 actions, 9 consumed. The two no-op ACTION7s didn't consume. So the timer only decreases on actions that change the board. Good.
Current character: columns 20-22, facing right (Y is on the right side at column 22).
Now, the goal. Let me think about what this game could be. Actually, this might be a game where the character is a "ball" that bounces around the maze, and the green blocks were "enemies" or "obstacles" that needed to be destroyed. After destroying them all… the level should complete. But it didn't.
Wait — did I destroy all the green blocks? Initially there were 7 N nodes. I destroyed 7 (1 + 6). Current frame: no N nodes. Yes, all destroyed.
Hmm, but maybe the level requires the character to also reach a goal. Or maybe the level completes when the character reaches the goal, and the green blocks were just obstacles on the path.
Where could the goal be? Let me think: the character is at rows 37-40. The goal might be at the top-left hole (rows 1-5, columns 13-16) — the first hole. But the character can't move vertically.
Or — wait. Maybe I'm misunderstanding the board. Let me re-verify: maybe the character can move vertically via ACTION7, but only when there's sky directly above (i.e., jumping up). In the pocket, above the character is the central bar (black). So ACTION7 (jump) fails. If the character is in a cell where the area above is sky, ACTION7 might move it up.
Let me test: move the character to cell 24-29 (RIGHT), where above is sky (rows 37-40, columns 24-29 is sky, and above that is rows 30-36… the central bar spans columns 13-42, rows 30-36. So above cell 24-29 is the central bar (black). Hmm.
What about cell 42-47 (columns 42-47)? The central bar ends at column 42, so above cell 42-47 is sky (rows 30-36, columns 43-53 is the sky gap). So if the character is at cell 42-47 (columns 44-46), above is sky. Then ACTION7 might jump up.
To get there: from columns 20-22, RIGHT×4 → columns 44-46. That's 4 actions. Then ACTION7.
But wait, is there anything blocking the character's path at rows 37-40, columns 24-47? All sky. The right column starts at column 54. So the character can move right up to cell 48-53 (columns 50-52), and then cell 54-59 is black (right column) — blocked?
Let me test the hypothesis: move RIGHT to cell 24-29, then ACTION7, and see if the character jumps.
Actually, a cheaper test: the character is currently at columns 20-22. Above is the central bar (black). ACTION7 failed. Let me move RIGHT once (to columns 26-28), then ACTION7. Above is still the central bar. Hmm, no good.
The central bar spans columns 13-42. So cells 18-23, 24-29, 30-35, 36-41 all have the bar above. Cell 42-47 (columns 42-47): the bar ends at column 42, so columns 43-47 have sky above. The character at columns 44-46 would have sky above. So I need RIGHT×4 to reach columns 44-46.
Or on the left side: cell 12-17 (columns 12-17): the bar starts at column 13. The character at columns 14-16: above (rows 30-36, columns 14-16) is the bar (black). So blocked.
Hmm, so the only cell with sky above is 42-47 (and beyond: 48-53, columns 48-53, sky above, and to the right is the right column).
Let me try: RIGHT×4, then ACTION7. If the character jumps up, I'll learn the mechanic.
Actually, wait — maybe ACTION7 isn't a jump. Let me reconsider. Maybe ACTION7 is "rotate" or "shoot." Or maybe the character needs to be on top of something.
Or, maybe the goal is simply to move the character to a specific cell, and the green blocks were just a distraction/obstacle. The goal cell might be marked by a hole: the top-left hole (rows 1-5, columns 13-16) is directly above… no, that's not right.
Hmm, let me look at the board from a "pipe" perspective: the black maze forms a path. The holes in the slab (rows 1-5, columns 13-16, 19-23, 25-29) — 3 holes in a row at the top. The central bar is at rows 30-36, columns 13-42. The pocket is at rows 37-41, columns 19-23.
Actually, you know what? Let me try a completely different hypothesis: this is a "ball in a maze" game, the ball is affected by gravity, and it's currently resting in the pocket. The pocket is a "cup." The green blocks were blocking the ball's path. Now, maybe I need to move the ball so it can fall through a gap into the lower area, and then… no, that's not it.
Let me try the RIGHT×4 + ACTION7 probe. 5 actions, 4 timer cost (if ACTION7 is a no-op it costs 0). Timer has 55 remaining. No problem.
Actually, let me be smarter: first just try RIGHT×1 + ACTION7 and see if ACTION7 does anything different in cell 24-29 (above is still the bar). No, that won't distinguish. Let me go straight to RIGHT×4 + ACTION7.
Wait, actually, let me reconsider whether the character can even pass through the pocket area. The character is at columns 20-22, inside the pocket (the black protrusion at columns 19-23, rows 37-41). If I press RIGHT, the character moves to columns 26-28 (sky). Let me verify that RIGHT works from the pocket (it did before: RIGHT returned the character to columns 20-22 from columns 14-16).
OK, let me execute RIGHT×4 + ACTION7 and observe.
